value.content: {"id": "portswigger_cache_poisoning", "item_type": "methodology", "topic": "web_cache_poisoning", "category": "PortSwigger Web Security: Web Cache Poisoning", "name": "Web Cache Poisoning via Unkeyed Inputs & Headers Methodology", "cwe": "CWE-444", "owasp_category": "A05:2021 - Security Misconfiguration", "signals": ["x_cache_hit_miss_header", "age_header_incrementing", "unkeyed_header_reflection", "x_forwarded_host_reflection", "fat_get_parameter_handling", "normalized_cache_key"], "verification_strategy": "Identify cache keys and caching status via headers (X-Cache: HIT/MISS, CF-Cache-Status). Inject non-standard headers (X-Forwarded-Host, X-Forwarded-Scheme, X-Original-URL) with benign markers to verify if the server reflects them and caches the resulting response for subsequent standard requests.", "evidence_requirements": ["cached_response_with_injected_header", "x_cache_hit_confirmation", "unkeyed_input_identification"], "tools": [{"tool": "Param Miner", "cmd": "param_miner.guess_headers(target_url)", "desc": "Automated unkeyed header and unkeyed cookie discovery engine"}, {"tool": "httpx", "cmd": "httpx -u url -probe-headers 'X-Cache,CF-Cache-Status,Age'", "desc": "Monitors cache header states across repeated requests"}], "remediation": "Do not incorporate unkeyed inputs into HTTP responses without encoding. Include necessary request headers in the cache key or disable caching for dynamically generated or personalized pages.", "description": "PortSwigger Web Cache Poisoning labs explore unkeyed header exploitation (X-Forwarded-Host), unkeyed cookies, DOM-based cache poisoning, multiple header coordination, and fat GET requests poisoning resource paths."}
